9. Shri. S. S. Koliwad, learned counsel for respondents submits that the copy of the driving license was not produced by the owner before the Tribunal which is necessitated the Tribunal to draw an adverse inference that the driver of the - 26 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3728 C/w.

10. He also submits that an opportunity needs to be provided to find out whether the driver of the lorry did possess a valid driving license as on the date of accident.
11. He further submits that even on the quantum of compensation the Tribunal has erred in not properly assessing the compensation for the death of sheep/goats.
12. He further contended that value of the each sheep/goat has been assessed by the Director of Animal Husbandry in a sum of Rs.7,000/- per sheep and per goat.
Whereas the Tribunal has granted exorbitant compensation without there being any proper material on record.

13. Therefore, he sought for remitting the matter for fresh disposal in accordance with law by affording suitable opportunity to find out the veracity of the driving license as well as the question of quantum of compensation.

15. Taking note of the fact that there is no proper assessment of the damages on the death or injury of the goats and sheep, and also question of liability is to be fastened on to the Insurance Company,
if there is a valid driving license, in the considered opinion of this Court matters require reconsideration at the hands of the Tribunal by affording suitable opportunity for the owner to produce the driving license and the Insurance Company to question the validity of driving license and also proper assessment of the damages.
